overview.description: Empat Satu (which means 'Forty-One' in Indonesian) is a fast-paced draw-andnd-discard card game popular throughout Southeast Asia. The game is a test of optimization where players manage a small 4-card hand, attempting to collect four cards of the same suit. The legendary '41' is achieved by holding an Ace and three 10ndvalue cards of the same suit. Because hands are small and the deck is large, the game moves rapidly, often ending in just a few turns when a player 'knocks' or declares a stop.

history.origins: Originating in Indonesia as a social card game, Empat Satu is widely played in coffee shops and community gatherings. Its simplicity makes it accessible across all age groups.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Becomes a staple Indonesian leisure game.
Modern Era: Digital versions and mobile apps bring the game to a global audience.
history.evolution: Derived from simpler matching games, it evolved to include a unique 'penalty' scoring system for hands with mixed suits.
history.cultural: Often played for small stakes or as a quick social filler between longer games.

setup.players: 2 to 4 players. Each plays for themselves.
setup.dealing: The dealer gives 4 cards to each player, one at a time. The rest of the deck forms the face-down Stock. The top card of the Stock is turned over to start the Discard Pile.

rules.objective: Collect four cards of the same suit to maximize your score (maximum 41).
rules.gameplay:
1. Turn: On your turn, you draw one card (from the Stock or the Discard Pile) and then discard one card face-up.
2. One-Card Limit: You must always have exactly 4 cards at the end of your turn.
3. The Stop: Any player who has four cards of the SAME SUIT can declare 'Stop' (Selesai). The hand ends immediately.
keyRules: You cannot pick up the previous player's discard and immediately discard it back.
If the Stock runs out, the discard pile is shuffled to form a new Stock.
If a player 'Stops' and their 4-card suit sum is lower than an opponent's mixed-hand sum, the stopper still wins the round in some house rules, but usually, the highest score wins regardless.

strategy.basic: Commit early. If you are dealt two high cards of the same suit (e.g., A and Q of Clubs), discard everything else and hunt for Clubs immediately.
strategy.intermediate: The Discard Signal: Pay attention to what your opponent discards. If they drop a King of Diamonds, itâ€™s a strong sign they are NOT collecting Diamonds. You can safely build a Diamond hand knowing they likely won't take your discards.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: If you know the player to your left is collecting Spades, you should hold onto high Spades even if they don't fit your hand, to prevent them from hitting 41.
tips: Don't wait for 41. If you have 38 or 39, it's often better to Stop before an opponent manages to fix a messy hand.
High cards (10s and Aces) are the only way to reach safe scores; dump low cards (2s and 3s) unless they are part of your core suit.

difficulty.easy: Collects cards randomly; fails to switch suits if the draw is unfavorable.
difficulty.medium: Identifies the highest-potential suit in the starting hand; blocks the next player's apparent suit.
difficulty.hard: Simulates opponent hand states based on discards; calculates the exact point at which to 'Stop' to maximize win probability against the field.

considerations: AI must handle the 'Stop' decision carefullyâ€”it's a classic greedy-optimization problem.

scoring.description:
1. Uniform Hand: If all 4 cards are the same suit, your score is the sum of their values (Max: 11+10+10+10 = 41).
2. Mixed Hand: If you have cards of different suits, your score is the sum of the suit you have the MOST points in, MINUS the sum of all other cards.
   *Example*: A-Hearts (11), K-Hearts (10), 2-Hearts (2), 10-Spades (10). Score = (11+10+2) - 10 = 13.
